---
title: "4 Governance: documenting a model with agents"
---

Session 4 is the finale. The platform works and every gate passes, but a validator would
still send its documentation back. This session is about why, and about writing
documentation a validator accepts, with an AI agent doing much of the drafting and every
claim checked against the repository.

## Why documentation fails validation

Most model documents fail review for the same few reasons, and none of them is about the
model:

- **They describe results, not decisions.** A table of metrics is not an account of
  intended use, alternatives considered, assumptions, limitations or monitoring.
- **Their numbers drift from the model.** A figure typed into a document is correct on the
  day it is typed. After the next refit it is a claim nobody rechecks.
- **They quote a metric without its population.** The same scorecard scores
  {{< var score.pop.everyone.auc >}} on all held-out applicants and
  {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} on the loans the bank books.
- **They do not raise their own findings.** A validator trusts a document that names its
  weaknesses more than one that has none.

## One source, two spines

This site is written once and read two ways. The **Course** tab is the path a learner
takes, session by session. The **Model Documentation** tab is the same platform in the
order US supervisory guidance (SR 11-7) expects, with a
[crosswalk](../reference/crosswalk.qmd) to OSFI E-23 and PRA SS1/23. The same source
also renders a versioned validation PDF.

Every number on every page is a named fact, recomputed by `python verify.py` through the
platform's own functions; a lint fails the build on any number typed by hand. See
[how to read this documentation](../mdd/index.qmd).

## D4: the worked example

The [Business Credit Score chapter, D4](../mdd/score/index.qmd), is complete. It follows the nine-part
[template](../mdd/index.qmd#the-template) — purpose, data, methodology, assumptions,
performance, sensitivity, limitations, monitoring, gate — and raises five open findings
about its own model, each with evidence, a compensating control and an owner.

## The lab: draft D5 with an agent (H4.1)

In pairs, pick one part of the template and have your agent draft it for D5, Loan
Adjudication, starting from the [chapter's stub](../mdd/adjudication/index.qmd). The draft
is done when it passes the lint — every number a fact, every fact resolving — and a
self-check confirms the part is complete. The lab needs no Quarto: the lint and the check
are plain Python.

Then turn the agent into a validator: have it review D4 and compare its findings with the
five the chapter raises.

## Homework with an agent

Three exercises: draft a D5 part (H4.1), review D4 as a validator (H4.2), and extend the
crosswalk for one module (H4.3). They arrive with the session, each with a self-check
where one is possible: [Session 4 homework](homework-s4.qmd).
